name: Thunder Compute

modes.label: GPU instances (on-demand, per GPU incl. base vCPU/RAM)
modes.note: Per-GPU price of the 1x bundle (https://www.thundercompute.com/pricing, 2026-09-28): H100 PCIe $3.20/h (4-16 vCPU, 32-128 GB), A100 80GB $1.09/h (8-16 vCPU, 64-128 GB), L40 $0.79/h (6-12 vCPU, 48-96 GB), RTX A6000 $0.35/h (6-8 vCPU, 48-64 GB), 100 GB disk included. The bundle includes the minimum vCPU count (4 H100 / 8 A100 / 6 L40, A6000) at 8 GB RAM per core; extra vCPU $0.04/vCPU-h is NOT modelled (vcpu_h 0), so workloads above the included vCPU are understated by $0.04 per extra vCPU-h. Billed per minute. H100 multi-GPU is linear (2x $6.40, 4x $12.80, 8x $25.60); A100/L40 at 4x/8x cost more per GPU than 1x (A100 4x $5.96, 8x $11.92; L40 4x $3.96, 8x $7.92), which the per-GPU price understates.

caveats: All prices are complete base GPU-instance bundles at the minimum CPU count, not stand-alone GPU surcharges. Minute billing; no egress charge.
Additional CPU $0.04/core-h, usually 8 GB RAM included per core. Running disk first 100 GB included then $0.03/100GB-h; stopped storage uses snapshots $0.05/GB-month.
Multi-GPU non-linear: 4×/8× A100 and L40 cost more per GPU than 1×/2×. Do not multiply single-GPU price blindly.

GPU mode priced per GPU from the 1x bundles (vcpu_h/ram_gib_h 0 because base CPU/RAM is bundled). Extra vCPU ($0.04/vCPU-h) beyond the bundle minimum is not modelled; A100/L40 4x and 8x bundles cost more per GPU than 1x (understated). Running disk beyond 100 GB: $0.03 per 100 GB-hour = $0.219/GB-month at 730 h.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

fleet.verification: Create account and add payment method.
fleet.notes: Official September 2026 provider article says no GPU quota approval required. No fixed aggregate fleet maximum published; fast single-instance launch claim is not a 1,000-instance stock guarantee.
